And the reason I call it the hot stove meditation is it has to do with this notion that when you literally touch a hot stove, there's a reflexive protective response, which is a really amazing part of the nervous system that it does that. But when it comes to other forms of pain, especially emotional pain, that reflexive avoidance or protective response is actually the opposite of what seems to be most healing. It's actually much more healing to metaphorically keep your hand on the hot stove of an uncomfortable emotional feeling so that you can notice the nature of it as body sensation and as energy.
